messages:
sam: Heads-up — invoice-preview alerts tripped for ~20 tenants at 04:12 UTC. Metering lag notifier kicked. Anyone digging in? :eyes:

billing-bot: ALERT: metering-lag-notifier triggered (count=19) for window 04:00-04:10 UTC. See /alerts/70872 for details.

mina: I noticed a cluster of enrich jobs delayed between 04:03-04:08. Preview pipeline shows 'enrich_timeout' for route-resolver. Some tenant previews landed with token_count=0 while raw events existed.

josh: putting a short paste of the tail logs from the enrich worker: ```
2026-03-21T04:05:12Z ERROR enrich-service route-resolver timeout tenant=acme-id req_id=xyz123 elapsed=5100ms
2026-03-21T04:05:13Z WARN  metering-ingest event queued tenant=acme-id seq=345
2026-03-21T04:06:02Z INFO  preview-generator reconcile attempt tenant=acme-id status=incomplete
```

irene: Sounds like a cascade: route-resolver slowdown -> enrich backlog -> invoice-preview sees partial/absent aggregates -> notifier noise. Two proposals: 1) give invoice-preview a visible 'last_ingest_ts' + health badge in Console so CS sees it's delayed rather than broken, OR 2) suppress notifier for transient windows under 5m to reduce paging.

sam: Agree on reducing noise. But suppressing at notifier layer worries me — we might hide real billing gaps. I lean toward Console UX first (badge + hover reason) + expose an internal status API we can query from clients and alerts. Minimal surface, e.g. GET /metering/status?tenant=xxx returning last_ingest_ts, pending_events, and watermark. Thoughts? :thinking:

mina: I like internal endpoint. Two caveats: (a) we must avoid coupling dashboards to hot internal counters that are expensive to compute, and (b) it should be authorization gated (billing teams + CS).

josh: Implemented a prototype earlier: /internal/metering/tenant_status (auth z only). It returns a tiny payload and reads from the same watermark store we use for reconciliation. Example: ```json
{"tenant":"acme-id","last_ingest_ts":"2026-03-21T04:06:02Z","watermark":"2026-03-21T03:58:00Z","pending_events":42}
```

irene: If we expose that, console can show a small banner: "Data freshness: 6m behind — invoice preview may be incomplete" with link to raw ingest traces. That keeps CS informed and avoids immediate oncall noise.

sam: How about telemetry/alerts integration: keep notifier but change severity to 'paging' only if last_ingest_ts < (now - 30m) OR pending_events > 10k. Otherwise downgrade to 'console-warning' and slack-first channel. That way brief slowdowns don't wake oncall.

mina: Works for me — simple policy. We'll need to version that logic in the notifier config and ship a canary. Also add a sampling flag so we still page for a small percentage of transient cases to detect false-negatives.

josh: Implementation notes: notifier currently runs as a CRON every 5m and queries aggregate windows. We can add the extra checks cheaply by hitting the watermark KV per tenant. Patch should be small. I can sketch a PR if we agree.

billing-bot: AUDIT: notifier-policy change proposed by sam at 2026-03-21T04:28Z. Automated runbook link: https://redwood-internal/runbooks/metering-lag.

irene: UX item — Console needs a hover tooltip explaining "last_ingest_ts vs watermark" and a link to tenancy-level ingest traces. Mina, can Design give a 1-pixel mock? Low effort.

mina: I'll ping design. Meanwhile Josh, if you can drop a tiny spec for the endpoint (url, required fields, auth scope, expected QPS) I can PR the notifier change and add Console hook.

josh: Will do this afternoon. Quick spec draft: GET /internal/metering/tenant_status?tenant_id=STRING -> { tenant, last_ingest_ts, watermark_ts, pending_events, sample_flag }. Auth: service/billing-read. QPS: <1000 global. Rate limit per tenant 1rps.

sam: Perfect. Let's run a 2-week canary rolling out notifier policy to 10% of tenants and add the Console banner for those tenants only. We'll collect metrics: page_count, slack-alerts, invoice-preview-deltas. If pages drop and preview deltas are low, expand.

mina: I'll file a canary tracking ticket and add the dashboard cards we need. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

sam: Thanks — appreciate the fast triage.
